Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
MykBuc wrote:
>
> If you had Anson and Parthenon in play could you use 3 Sudden Reversals
> out-of-turn?
>

> Mike

The rules only allow a player to play one out-of-turn master each turn
no matter how many master phase actions that player has at his/her
disposal. After playing your one OOT Master, you would still be able to
take 2 other master phase actions during your next master phase.

Robert

myk...@aol.com (MykBuc) wrote:
>If you had Anson and Parthenon in play could you use 3 Sudden Reversals
>out-of-turn?
>

>Mike

As far as I can tell, No! The Partheon states that you can tap DURING
YOUR MASTER PHASE to get an extra master phase action. This excludes
using it out of turn.

Hmmmm. Are you positive about this? Not to be contradictory (even
though the Design Team is), I have to wonder about this.

There used to be a ruling that a Master-Out-Of-Turn substituted for
your entire Master Phase, but the tournament this weekend was using
the OOT as a Master action. This allowed you an OOT and a Master if
you had Anson, Parthenon or Rumors in effect.

So, if you could OOT and Master in the same turn, why not 2 OOT's?
Mind you, I'd hate to see this, but it does seem logical. As if the
rulings and errata were logical ;)

Darby

>James Hamblin <je...@cornell.edu> wrote:
>>Just to be clear, you can only ever play one OOT master per turn (around
>>the table). Even if you have Anson, you don't get another chance until
>>it's been your turn again.

>Hmmmm. Are you positive about this? Not to be contradictory (even
>though the Design Team is), I have to wonder about this.

(3.2.1)
Once you've played an out-of-turn master card, you can't play
another one until after your next turn.

>There used to be a ruling that a Master-Out-Of-Turn substituted for

That wasn't a ruling - that was in the rules for Jyhad.

>your entire Master Phase, but the tournament this weekend was using
>the OOT as a Master action. This allowed you an OOT and a Master if
>you had Anson, Parthenon or Rumors in effect.

When the new rules (VtES) came out, they added the concept of Master
Phase Action. Normally, you get only one. They also added the rule
that you can only play one MOoT between your turns.

Messages.Author: James Puzzo
Messages.Body:
Darby Keeney (dke...@amgen.com) wrote:
:
: There used to be a ruling that a Master-Out-Of-Turn substituted for
: your entire Master Phase, but the tournament this weekend was using

: the OOT as a Master action. This allowed you an OOT and a Master if
: you had Anson, Parthenon or Rumors in effect.

:
: So, if you could OOT and Master in the same turn, why not 2 OOT's?

: Mind you, I'd hate to see this, but it does seem logical. As if the
: rulings and errata were logical ;)

The reasoning, as I understand it, is that these cards which allow extra
master "actions" may no longer be under your control (burned, stolen,
whatever) by the time it becomes your turn again. Therefore, you are
only allowed to use the one master action that you are guaranteed
"before" it's your turn.

-spongy
